20-384 kcal per 100g {{cite web|title=The Food Database|url=http://www7.slv.se/Naringssok/Naringsamnen.aspx|publisher=National Food Administration (Sweden)|access-date=15 June 2012|pages="Rosehip soup ready-to-eat powder unsweetened fortified" and "Rosehip soup dried powder fortified"|language=sv, en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120818030008/http://www7.slv.se/Naringssok/Naringsamnen.aspx|archive-date=18 August 2012}} | other = }} [[File:Drying of Rose hips for tea (1).JPG|thumb|Rose hips]] '''Rose hip soup''' ({{langx|sv|nyponsoppa}}) is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] soup made from [[rose hip]]s.{{cite news |title=Rose Hip Soup Recipe |url=http://homecooking.about.com/od/fruitrecipes/r/blfruit8.htm |access-date=29 March 2020 |work=About.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816060858/http://homecooking.about.com:80/od/fruitrecipes/r/blfruit8.htm |archive-date=16 August 2016}} It is served as a beverage or as a [[dessert]] with [[milk]], [[cream]] or [[vanilla]] [[ice cream]] along with small almond biscuits. Rose hip soup may be eaten for breakfast. The types of soup for that purpose are generally lower in fruit content and more watery, and may be served with pieces of [[Crispbread|crisp bread]].
